The relationship between Fan Li (范蠡) and A Qing (阿青) is multifaceted, evolving through interactions marked by mentorship, mutual care, emotional attachment, and eventual conflict. Initially, Fan Li speaks to and invites A Qing, and he inquires about her swordplay master, showing interest in her martial skills. Fan Li appreciates and admires A Qing, and he becomes infatuated with her, spending time with her daily as she tends to her sheep. He cares for her deeply, searching for her when she is missing and protecting her, while A Qing in turn protects Fan Li from attacks by a white ape.

Emotionally, Fan Li regards A Qing as a little sister and a close friend, while A Qing harbors strong feelings of admiration and dependence toward Fan Li, trusting him completely. However, their relationship takes a dramatic turn when A Qing attempts to kill Xi Shi (西施), Fan Li’s beloved, placing her in direct opposition to Fan Li. This act of violence creates a fundamental rift, transforming their bond from one of affection and loyalty into a confrontation driven by jealousy and conflicting loyalties.
